ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: According to the schematic diagram “changes in coal and iron required for smelting one ton of steel,” read the figure and answer: <image1> By 1985, steel industries were mostly located at ports rather than at iron ore producing areas. What was the main reason in terms of traffic conditions?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows that in “changes in coal and iron required for smelting one ton of steel,” the unit consumption of coal decreased from about 4 tons in 1800 to about 2 tons in 1900, and then to less than 1 ton in 1985; the unit consumption of iron ore also decreased from about 2 tons in 1800 to more than about 1 ton in 1985. By 1985, the quantities of coal and iron ore required for smelting one ton of steel had both clearly decreased. The question is limited to analysis from the “traffic conditions aspect,” and compares “ports” and “iron ore producing areas.” Because the unit consumption of raw materials decreased, the steel industry no longer had to be located close to iron ore producing areas; while ports have the transportation advantages of convenient shipping and transshipment, facilitating the transportation of raw materials and products. Therefore the main reason can be summarized as convenient transportation.
